findings.title: 78-95% of MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq test items are in the Math10K training data
findings.claim: The Math10K fine-tuning file (ft-training_set/math_10k.json, 9919 items) is built from GSM8K + MAWPS + MAWPS-single + 1000 AQuA (README l.48; paper 3.2). Because MAWPS aggregates AddSub/MultiArith/SingleEq, 569/600 (94.8%) MultiArith, 331/395 (83.8%) AddSub and 449/508 (88.4%) SingleEq test questions in dataset/*/test.json appear verbatim (alnum-normalized) in the training file, with the same numeric answers and a worked solution in the 'output' field; GSM8K/AQuA/SVAMP show 0%.
findings.concern: The paper's headline claim that LLaMA-13B+LoRA 'outperforms GPT-3.5 on MultiArith, AddSub, and SingleEq' (intro finding 2; 4.2) and that PEFT is 'successfully applied to OOD datasets' (4.4) is invalidated: those three test sets are in the fine-tuning data, so Table 3 measures memorisation, not generalisation, on exactly the datasets used to support the conclusion.
findings.resolution: Re-evaluate on the MAWPS-disjoint variant (the shipped math_7k.json/math_14k.json remove MAWPS, per README l.48) and report MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq only under a train-disjoint split, or drop them; confirm which math_*.json produced Table 3.
findings.reason: check_train_test_contamination.py reproduced independently gives identical numbers (MultiArith 569/600=94.8%, AddSub 331/395=83.8%, SingleEq 449/508=88.4%, GSM8K/AQuA/SVAMP 0%); README.md:47-48 'Special Announcement' explicitly confirms math_10k.json is built from GSM8K+MAWPS+AQuA(1000) and warns MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq can't be used as eval sets with it; paper_text.txt confirms the cited 'outperforms GPT-3.5 on MultiArith, AddSub, and SingleEq' (p.8) and 'successfully applied to OOD datasets' (4.4) claims verbatim.

findings.title: 4.4 says Math10K 'only includes GSM8K and AQuA', contradicting 3.2 and the data
findings.quote: the fine-tuning data set, Math10K, only includes the training sets of GSM8K and AQuA
findings.claim: Section 4.4 states Math10K contains only GSM8K and AQuA training sets and uses this to frame MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq as OOD. Section 3.2 says Math10K also incorporates 'the training sets from GSM8K, MAWPS, MAWPS-single ... and 1000 examples from AQuA', and the shipped ft-training_set/math_10k.json indeed contains MAWPS-derived items (see math10k-mawps-test-contamination).
findings.concern: The 4.4 description of the training data is factually wrong and is precisely what makes the leakage invisible to a reader: it labels in-distribution (memorised) datasets as OOD.
findings.resolution: Correct 4.4 to state Math10K includes MAWPS/MAWPS-single, and reclassify MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq accordingly (they are ID, not OOD).
findings.paper_ref: 4.4 (ID and OOD Analysis) vs 3.2 (Fine-tuning Data Collection)
findings.reason: Quote 'the fine-tuning data set, Math10K, only includes the training sets of GSM8K and AQuA' found verbatim in paper_text.txt (4.4); section 3.2 (paper_text.txt:499) confirms Math10K also incorporates MAWPS/MAWPS-single, and README.md's Special Announcement confirms the same, so the 4.4 description does contradict 3.2 and the actual data.

findings.title: requirements.txt has zero version pins and installs transformers from git main
findings.quote:
accelerate
appdirs
bitsandbytes
black
black[jupyter]
datasets
fire
git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
gradio
findings.claim: No dependency carries a version constraint, and transformers is pulled from an unpinned git main. The repo vendors its own 2023-era peft (peft/src/) that patches specific transformers internals; a current transformers main is not guaranteed to be compatible.
findings.concern: The exact environment that produced Tables 3-4 cannot be rebuilt, and PEFT results are known to be sensitive to transformers/peft versions, so re-runs may silently diverge or fail to import.
findings.resolution: Pin transformers (and peft/accelerate/bitsandbytes/datasets) to the exact versions/commit used for the paper, e.g. via a frozen requirements lock.
findings.reason: requirements.txt lines 1-9 match the quote verbatim: no version pins on any package, transformers installed via 'git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git'; repo does vendor its own peft/src/ tree.

findings.title: No code reproduces the ChatGPT commonsense baseline (headline comparison)
findings.quote: we employ the gpt-3.5-turbo API with a zero-shot CoT
findings.claim: The headline claim 'LLaMA-13B with Parallel Adapter ... a 4.5% improvement over ChatGPT' (4.3) rests on ChatGPT numbers the authors computed via the gpt-3.5-turbo API. The repo's two evaluators (evaluate.py, commonsense_evaluate.py) only load a fine-tuned PeftModel; no script queries the API, and no raw ChatGPT outputs are stored.
findings.concern: A headline comparison depends on a nondeterministic commercial API with no code and no saved predictions, so the ChatGPT column of Table 4 is not reproducible or auditable.
findings.resolution: Ship the API-query script (prompt template, model snapshot date, decoding params) and the raw ChatGPT predictions used for Table 4.
findings.reason: Quote 'we employ the gpt-3.5-turbo API with a zero-shot CoT' found verbatim in paper_text.txt (4.3); repo-wide search finds no openai/api_key/gpt-3.5-turbo API-querying code anywhere (only unrelated fine-tuning-data text mentions 'OpenAI'), no file named *chatgpt*, and evaluate.py/commonsense_evaluate.py import only PeftModel/transformers classes, confirming no API-query script or raw ChatGPT outputs are shipped.

findings.title: Trained adapters for the 32 reported result rows are not in the repo
findings.quote: * [2023-04-21] We released math10k dataset and the [LLaMA-13B adapter checkpoints](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NqUv-Hn_mAkGXsUOqpJKmPKW5Gp8mRlO/view?usp=sharing). The LLaMA-13B-Parallel model achieves **91%** of GPT-3.5 performance!
findings.claim: Only a subset of LLaMA-13B adapter checkpoints is linked, and only via an external Google Drive URL. No trained_models/ or experiment/ artefacts exist in the repo (find for *.bin/*.pt/*.safetensors returns nothing), so 30+ of the 32 Table 3/4 model×adapter configs have no weights available.
findings.concern: Reproducing the tables requires retraining every configuration (gated LLaMA weights, multi-GPU, hours each), and the one provided checkpoint set sits behind an unversioned external link, weakening verifiability.
findings.resolution: Provide (or archive with a DOI) the adapter checkpoints for all reported configurations, or a manifest mapping each Table 3/4 row to a downloadable artefact.
findings.reason: README.md:43 quote matches verbatim (single Google-Drive-hosted LLaMA-13B checkpoint link); repo-wide search for *.bin/*.pt/*.safetensors/*.ckpt and for trained_models/experiment directories returns nothing, confirming no other configs' weights are shipped.

findings.title: AQuA scorer returns the first capital A-E anywhere in the generation
findings.claim: For AQuA the predicted option is pred_answers[0], i.e. the FIRST capital A-E character in the whole CoT output. A stray capital letter in the rationale (a sentence starting with 'Add'->A, 'Between'->B, 'Divide'->D, 'Each'->E) is returned instead of the final choice; _audit_code/check_aqua_letter_extraction.py shows 4 realistic outputs mis-scored. This is inconsistent with the sibling extract_answer_number, which takes the LAST match (pred[-1]).
findings.concern: The Table 3 AQuA column can be mis-scored (usually downward) by rationale text; the accuracy reported for AQuA is not a faithful measure of whether the model chose the correct option.
findings.resolution: Extract the letter adjacent to an answer cue (e.g. after 'answer is'/'option'), or take the last A-E match, mirroring extract_answer_number.
findings.reason: evaluate.py:290-298 matches the quote verbatim (re.findall + pred_answers[0], i.e. first A-E match); extract_answer_number (line 279) does use pred[-1], confirming the described inconsistency; re-running check_aqua_letter_extraction.py verbatim reproduces the claimed 4/5 mis-scored realistic examples.
